newsitem.title: LEBANON: Mideast talks must resume on Madrid basis - Primakov.
newsitem.headline: Mideast talks must resume on Madrid basis - Primakov.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said in Beirut on Tuesday that stalled Arab-Israeli peace talks should resume on the basis of the land-for-peace formula adopted at the 1991 Madrid conference.

"We either stick to the founding principles and agreements in this lengthy process or each government will take new stands and prevent the continuity of the Middle East peace process," he told reporters after talks with Lebanese counterpart Faris Bouez.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said that he rejects the resumption of peace talks with Lebanon and Syria on the basis of exchanging occupied Arab land for peace, namely the Golan Heights seized from Syria in 1967. Israel also occupies a border strip in south Lebanon since 1985.
Primakov arrived in Beirut from Damascus on Tuesday on the second leg of a Middle East tour to seek a more active Russian role in the American-dominated Arab-Israeli peace process.
"We are not trying to go against the Americans. We want to complete the existing orchestra," he said.

Asked if he discussed with Syrian President Hafez al-Assad any specific proposals to push forward the peace process, Primakov replied: "I will not reveal at a news conference the new proposals or those that might come up".
Primakov -- who signed with Bouez an economic cooperation protocol between Lebanon and Russia -- is due to meet President Elias Hrawi and Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri later.
Primakov said at the airport that his country backs the implementation of the 1978 Security Council Resolution 425 calling for an immediate and unconditional Israeli withdrawal from south Lebanon.
He will leave Beirut on Wednesday and will visit Egypt, Jordan, Israel and the Palestinian self-ruled areas.
